note: Inconsistencies that have been traced to a cause and are tolerated until the
date below. The consistency check fails only on findings that are new or whose
entry here has expired, so this file is what keeps a known-and-explained
condition from turning the check permanently red.
Every entry carries an owner and an expiry on purpose: an exception nobody owns
and that never expires cannot be told apart from a finding nobody intends to fix.
When a date passes, the finding comes back as `expired` and the check fails until
All thirteen share one cause. Both findings compare the stored points against
something that only describes the *current* generation: the chunks endpoint lists
the active generation, and the knowledge-space check needs a stored copy carrying
metadata.knowledge_base_id. These documents were ingested before generation-scoped
writes existed, so their points carry no document_version_id, no generation_id and,
for the space-key cases, no metadata at all. The store keeps every generation by
design, so the legacy copy is expected to sit beside the current one rather than
under it. Rewriting those points would mean re-ingesting the documents, which
changes their doc_id and breaks every citation that names them.
